headline: Google has paused its open source bug bounty program until next year because of a flood of automated, mostly invalid AI-generated reports.
score_reason: Pool score kept: Google confirmed it; a notable sign of AI strain on security reporting.
importance_line: Independent researchers lose a paid route for reporting flaws in Google's open source software and maintainers lose a check on bugs, while Google says only that it will update in early 2027.
summary: TechCrunch reports that Google paused its Open Source Software Vulnerability Rewards Program on 1 Oct 2026, which paid researchers for finding security flaws in its open source code, citing 'a significant rise in automated submissions, the vast majority of which are not valid'. Google promised an update in the first quarter of 2027, and TechCrunch, citing Tom's Hardware, says engineers were swamped by invalid or hallucinated reports.
